newsitem.title: CANADA: CN, CP seek to outsource 30 jobs.
newsitem.headline: CN, CP seek to outsource 30 jobs.

text.p: Canadian National Railway Co and Canadian Pacific Ltd said on Tuesday they will jointly solicit bids for the repair, assembly and overhaul services of their system-wide train control and communications equipment.
That work was being provided by separate CN and CPR (Canadian Pacific Railway) facilities in Winnipeg, employing a total of 30 people.
It would be the first time CN and CPR have initiated a joint request for proposals, the railways said.
"I am very pleased to work together with our CPR colleagues as we seek to reduce our mutual operating expenses," CN's President and Chief Executive Officer Paul Tellier said in a statement.

"Both we and CN recognize that, to be competitive in the rapidly changing marketplace resulting from U.S. railway mega-mergers, we are going to have to cooperate to rationalize costly duplicate facilities or facilities that aren't part of our core business," said Robert Ritchie, CPR's President and Chief Executive Officer.
"I fully expect that we will find other opportunities for cooperation and that these will occur sooner rather than later," he said.

Advertisements soliciting interest will appear in national and trade newspapers and publications beginning June 6. The deadline for receipt of detailed proposals is the end of July, after which the consulting firm of KMPG chartered accountants will evaluate the bids, the railways said.
CN and CPR are Canada's two national freight railways. ((Reuters Montreal bureau 514-985-2434))
